text.title: RACI AI Assisted Output Contract
text.summary: Draft-07 JSON Schema for `RACIMatrix`: a roster and open-leaf snapshot, one row per open WBS leaf with exactly one accountable role id, an evidence anchor per anchored row, a `proposed` / `orphaned` status that blocks publish, the roster-delta diff with its deadline, and a `review_log` whose publish entries carry the notification record and whose quarterly entries carry the review counts. Validator: `scripts/validate-raci-ai-assisted.py`; staleness: `scripts/staleness-check.py`.

section.title: JSON Schema (draft-07)
section.note: What the validator's cross-field block checks beyond the schema: every open leaf in `wbs_open_leaves` has a row and no row's `wbs_id` is the parent of another row's (r-rows-bind-to-wbs-leaves); rows for leaves no longer open are rejected only when `trigger` is `quarterly_review`, since closed leaves are removed at the review and not earlier; every role id in R / A / C / I is in `roster`, and a row naming a role that is not is `orphaned` (r-responsible-in-roster); a role appears in at most one column per row, and a row whose C list is longer than its R list carries `over_consultation_reviewed: true` (r-one-column-per-role-per-row); for a `roster_delta`, `refresh_deadline` is `effective_date` for a leave or role change and `effective_date` + 7 days for a join, and `last_reviewed` is not after it (r-trigger-enum-and-roster-delta); on a published matrix the latest publish entry's recipients cover every role holding R or A (r-notify-assignees-on-publish); a quarterly entry's `rows_still_proposed` equals the count of `proposed` rows (r-quarterly-review-90-days). The 90-day staleness window is time-relative and is checked by `scripts/staleness-check.py`, not by the contract.

example.note: Subject violations: `accountable: "backend-lead, pm"` is two roles, not one role id (r-exactly-one-accountable-per-row); a row for the summary node `2` and no row for open leaf `2.2` (r-rows-bind-to-wbs-leaves); `security-lead` is not in the roster and the rows are not `orphaned`, while `pm` sits in both C and I on the same row (r-responsible-in-roster, r-one-column-per-role-per-row); an `anchored` row with no evidence and a `proposed` row on a published matrix (r-evidence-anchor-per-assignment); trigger `roster_delta` without the `roster_delta` diff (r-trigger-enum-and-roster-delta); a publish entry with no notification record (r-notify-assignees-on-publish).

antipattern.description: `accountable` containing a separator, empty, equal to `team` / `tbd` / `various`, or naming the agent or an automation.
antipattern.reason: r-exactly-one-accountable-per-row: two accountable roles are each one's assumption about the other; zero is the PM.

antipattern.description: Any R / A / C / I value absent from `roster`, or a row for a departed role not marked `orphaned`, or an `orphaned` row on a published matrix.
antipattern.reason: r-responsible-in-roster: the matrix rots at offboarding; eleven rows naming a lead who left is a month with nobody accountable for auth.

antipattern.description: A `wbs_id` that is the parent of another row's `wbs_id`, or an entry of `wbs_open_leaves` with no row.
antipattern.reason: r-rows-bind-to-wbs-leaves: a row for "2. Backend" hides that 2.3 has no owner.

antipattern.description: `header.status: published` with any row `proposed`, or an `anchored` row whose `evidence` is empty or does not match `charter#`, `wbs-dict#` or `stakeholders#`.
antipattern.reason: r-evidence-anchor-per-assignment: a plausible A without an anchor looks decided and nobody remembers deciding it.

antipattern.description: `header.trigger` outside `kickoff` / `roster_delta` / `quarterly_review`, a `roster_delta` trigger without the diff, or `last_reviewed` after `refresh_deadline`.
antipattern.reason: r-trigger-enum-and-roster-delta: "refresh when needed" refreshes never; the deadline is the person's last day.

antipattern.description: A role in two columns of one row, or a C list longer than the R list without `over_consultation_reviewed: true`.
antipattern.reason: r-one-column-per-role-per-row: a security lead in C on forty rows blocks forty deliverables or ignores forty notifications.

antipattern.description: A `publish` entry in `review_log` without `notification`, or recipients that do not cover every role holding R or A.
antipattern.reason: r-notify-assignees-on-publish: an assignment nobody was told about is not an assignment.

antipattern.description: `last_reviewed` older than 90 days (staleness-check.py), a `quarterly_review` trigger with no `quarterly_review` entry, or an entry whose `rows_still_proposed` disagrees with the rows.
antipattern.reason: r-quarterly-review-90-days: the counts are what tell the PM whether the same eleven rows have been proposed for two quarters.

text.reference: Stdlib-only validator for this contract; `--self-test` runs both examples above.
Flags a matrix whose `header.last_reviewed` is older than 90 days.
Markdown skeleton with the same header fields and row columns.
